highlights.title: Glucose Bobble contact image for Contact Trick
changes: Adds a new "Glucose Bobble" contact image layout for the Contact Trick feature.
The Bobble shows a ring, a color-coded glucose number, and a rotating trend arrow.
You can toggle showing minutes-since-reading and showing the glucose delta beneath the number.
You can switch the glucose number between color and monochrome modes.
When Bobble is selected, other contact-image customization options are hidden and stale CGM readings are cleared so the.

highlights.title: Fix bolus and carb label positioning on iOS 27
changes: Bolus and carbohydrate amount labels now appear next to their triangle markers in the chart.
This fixes label misplacement that occurred when building with Xcode 27 / iOS 27.
Marker triangles look the same; only the label anchoring was adjusted.

includedPullRequests.title: Adding Glucose Bobble as an optional "Contact Trick" image design.
includedPullRequests.body: While testing out the direct Dexcom driver for Trio, I found myself missing the Dexcom widget on my Apple Watch. I usually have it positioned as a very visible glucose badge. I enabled the "Contact Trick" feature and saw that the existing design templates could use some love. As an _optional feature_ I added the possibility to select a new layout called "Glucose Bobble" **(image 1)**. When selected, the rest of the options are hidden and replaced with separate options: Color Mode, show/hide minutes since last reading, and show/hide delta value. **(image 2)** After testing it for a while I found that colored glucose values have lower readability at night (without glasses...) so I added an option to change between colors and monochrome. **(image 3)**. Finally I added some information to the (i) sheet. **(Image 4)** This might all be replaced by a future direct-to-watch integration, but for now I think it deserves a place as an optional design choice.

includedPullRequests.title: Anchor bolus and carb amount labels to a zero-size companion mark
includedPullRequests.body:
resolves #1488 

This seems to just be an Apple bug when building to iOS 27 from Xcode 27. I tried several methods to address it but this is the only one I found that works — attaching the annotation to a different PointMark at the same location of the triangle.

Tested with the RC of both iOS 27 and Xcode 27.
